note: The provenance manifest for the vertical corpus (V2.3 item 6.4, issue A). Every document is REAL and PUBLIC. Model-written fixtures are cleaner and more internally consistent than real documents, which flatters the system and produces a corpus that proves nothing, so nothing here was written for the corpus. `fetch.mjs` re-downloads the originals from these URLs into `originals/` (gitignored) and verifies each `sha256`. The bytes are never committed: a URL plus a checksum is a stronger provenance record than a copied file, and the originals total about 27 MB, which does not belong in a source repository. What IS committed is the verbatim text excerpt each case runs on, produced by Cogeto's own reader from these bytes and never edited. Every licence below permits redistribution of the work in whole or in part; a document whose licence did not would have been referenced by URL with no excerpt committed, and none was needed.

documents.title: RP2040 Datasheet: A microcontroller by Raspberry Pi
documents.byte_stable_note: Raspberry Pi rebuilds this datasheet in place; the colophon carries a build date and version. The checksum records the build read on the retrieval date, and fetch.mjs warns rather than fails when it moves.
documents.licence: Creative Commons Attribution-NoDerivatives 4.0 International (CC BY-ND 4.0), as stated in the document colophon. Copyright 2020-2025 Raspberry Pi Ltd.
documents.why: CC BY-ND 4.0 grants the right to reproduce and share the licensed material IN WHOLE OR IN PART, and states that adapted material is never produced merely by technical modification, which is what extracting the text layer is. It forbids sharing ADAPTED material, so the committed excerpts are verbatim reader output and MUST NOT be edited, tidied, or paraphrased. A case that needs different text needs a different excerpt, not an edited one.
exercises: electrical characteristics tables flattened by a PDF text layer
numeric tolerances, ranges and typical/min/max columns
conditional qualification on one side (at IOVDD=1.8V)
shared boilerplate with the successor part

documents.licence: Reuse authorised under Commission Decision 2011/833/EU; EUR-Lex legal notice.
documents.croatian_origin_note: STATED PLAINLY: this is the Croatian authentic language version of an act drafted in English and French. Under EU law every language version is equally authentic, so it is not a machine translation and not an unofficial one, but it is still a translation and it reads like one. It is included because the cross-language entity work needs the SAME act in both languages, and it is labelled here so nobody mistakes it for Croatian-origin material. The Croatian-origin documents in this corpus are the two Narodne novine regulations and the Croatian contracting authority's tender notice.
exercises: the same obligations as the English act, for cross-language entity pairing
Croatian legal register
a real divergence from the English text in Article 10(7) cross-references
